correctness.rationale: Walsh rank-one spectral decomposition gives the two persistent double eigenspaces and three simple moving roots; PBH rank on double modes requires transverse parity, and an impossible two-vertex-support eigenvector proves visibility of moving modes. The t=1 triplet is explicitly certified. 252 rational pair ranks plus homogeneous case replayed as supplementary evidence. Proof is all t>0 and not extrapolated from enumeration.

evidence: Yuan et al. give a maximum-eigenvalue-multiplicity benchmark for freely chosen controls, not a coordinate-input placement census. Monshizadeh et al. address strong controllability over matrices sharing a graph pattern. An indexed all-dimensions unweighted hypercube actuator theorem uses no exceptional edge.

Yazıcıoğlu et al. prove a graph-distance lower bound valid for every positive edge weighting. As every pair fails at t=1 on Q3, that weight-invariant lower bound cannot imply full rank only at nonunit t.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither an unrestricted input-matrix multiplicity criterion nor an unweighted all-cube result implies that any particular two coordinate vectors span every eigenspace at every positive detuning. The construction and exact iff rank test are additional.

value.rationale: Complete and weight-uniform placement classification on a canonical eight-vertex, three-dimensional symmetric network resolves an actual sensor/actuator design choice. The parity criterion and discontinuous 3-to-2 actuator transition follow from nontrivial spectral coupling, not merely enumeration or a general multiplicity bound. Applicability is deliberately limited to one exceptional positive edge.
